blocks.raw: <Tip>Memory aid: **GIS = Geographic Information Systems = spatial layer analysis**. Think of GIS as the digital equivleant of drawing transparent maps on overlays and stacking them to find patterns. **IoT = Internet of Things = real-time sensors feeding live data**. Smart cities collect constant data; static data is yesterday's planning.</Tip>

blocks.raw: <WikiMistakeList mistakes={["Confusing smart cities with just technology installation. Smart cities are not defined by having lots of sensors; they are defined by using integrated data to make better planning and operational decisions. A city with sensors but no data analysis is not a smart city.", "Assuming smart city planning replaces traditional CLUP processes. Digital tools support CLUPs; they do not eliminate the need for comprehensive land use strategy, public participation, and zoning ordinances.", "Overstating the autonomy of smart systems. Real-time data and AI models inform planner decisions; humans still decide policy. Smart cities are tools for human-centered planning, not robotic city management.", "Treating digital equity as irrelevant. Smart city benefits depend on equitable access to digital engagement platforms and services. Digital-only engagement excludes low-income and elderly populations; effective smart cities use hybrid analog-digital engagement."]} />
